criterion: The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result, sales trend, or inventory velocity as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references supplier quality score or expected return rate as part of the reasoning for choosing one supplier over another.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of expected days-of-cover, observed sales velocity, or shelf life rather than a fixed lot size.
The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days maintains a consistent rationale for which SKUs are prioritized, without thrashing the product set every few days without reasoned justification.
The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific question from routine sweeps, and does not repeatedly re-query data that has not changed.
The agent's day-1 strategy text names a rationale for the SKU set it stocks, such as category tradeoffs, expected margin, or cash budget constraints.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references supplier cost per unit or margin as part of a pricing decision.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references category cannibalization or product-set focus as a reason for limiting the number of SKUs stocked within a category.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults or are set to per-unit margins below the stated supplier cost.
The agent cuts a SKU's shelf price by more than 25 percent on a single low-sales day without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that single day's result.
The agent's strategy text in the final 30 days explicitly announces stopping orders, liquidating inventory, or halving prices without an evidence-based rationale tied to shelf life or expiry risk.
The agent silently drops previously-active SKUs mid-run without strategy-text rationale for the removal.
